title: Note: reading a ghost story, part 3
summary: The scariest scene so far, with several earlier structures in real use.

blocks.text: Part 3 of the ghost story. Inside the house, the scene gets tense, and a lot of what you have learned turns up in real use. Read first, then check each phrase in the table at the end.
Here is what has happened in the story so far, in a few short lines.

blocks.jp: 部屋には誰もおらず、電気がついていた。
blocks.en: No one was in the room, and the light was on.

blocks.jp: どうやら、誰かが先に電気をつけたらしい。
blocks.en: Apparently someone had turned the light on first.

blocks.jp: 部屋の奥で、白い着物の女の人が寝てしまっていた。
blocks.en: At the back of the room, a woman in a white kimono had fallen asleep.

blocks.jp: 美咲は起こそうかと思ったが、そっとしておくことにした。
blocks.en: Misaki thought about waking her, but decided to leave her alone.

blocks.jp: その時、美咲は、窓の白い顔が女の人の顔ではなかったのを思い出した。
blocks.en: At that moment Misaki remembered that the white face in the window had not been this woman's face.

blocks.text: ついている vs つける
電気がついている means the light is on, as a state. 電気をつける means to switch it on, as an action. Which verb you see tells you whether someone acted or the light simply is on.
電気がついていた。 The light was on.
（誰かが）電気をつけた。 (Someone) switched the light on.
おらず: old いる + old ない

おらず has two parts. おる is an older, written form of いる, and it acts like a godan verb. ず is the old negative ending, a little like ない. Together they mean "was not (there), and ...", joining two clauses.
Phrases from earlier lessons in the wild

どうやら … らしい is the guess of lesson 25. 寝てしまった is the helper しまう of lesson 44. 起こそうかと思った is the volitional (lesson 17) + か (lesson 39) + と (the quoted thought). And そっとしておくことにした chains two lessons: ておく (lesson 21) and ことにする (lesson 29).
